The component never sees unmatched entries — it receives only the entries that should render.\\n\\n**Resolution logic by page context:**\\n\\n|  |  |  |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| **Page Context** | **ID Source** | **Match Logic** |\\n| PLP (category page) | Route param / SFCC category API response | Filter CDA entries where sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId OR sfccCategoryId is null (show-on-all). |\\n| PDP (product page) | Route param productId (master product ID) | Filter CDA entries where sfccProductId === currentProductId OR sfccProductId is null. |\\n| Homepage | No SFCC ID context | No ID filtering — all entries for the slot are rendered in authored order. |\\n| Campaign landing | Slug / experience ID | Filtered by Contentful Studio Experience — no SFCC ID filtering needed. |\\n\\n**Pseudocode — MRT SSR filter (PLP example):**\\n\\nconst allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({   content\\\\_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',   locale: currentLocale, });  const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter(entry => {   const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;   // null = show on all categories; specific ID = scoped render   return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId; });  // Only matched entries are passed to the component return <PlpInlineGridInsert entries={matchedInserts} />;\\n\\n### Cache Key Requirements\\n\\nThis is a critical implication of the ID-based filtering pattern. --------

Editorial and CMS content in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team. MRT (Managed Runtime — Salesforce's PWA hosting layer) acts as the integration layer between Contentful and the browser-rendered PWA storefront.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Direction** | **Flow** |
| Inbound (Contentful → MRT) | Published content entries (hero banners, editorial modules, navigation, footer, announcement banners, size guides, accordion copy) delivered via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA) to the MRT SSR layer on every page render. |
| Outbound (MRT → Contentful) | Cache-purge webhook acknowledgements; Management API calls from CI for schema migrations. No content flows from SFCC back to Contentful. |
| NOT in this flow | SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly. All CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. |

*Contentful is the sole CMS for all eight Zimmermann storefronts. SFCC manages commerce data (products, pricing, orders); Contentful manages editorial data (copy, imagery configuration, page layouts). They complement each other without overlap.*

Integration Architecture & Data Flow
------------------------------------

**Pattern:** Contentful → MRT (Node/SSR) → browser, SSR-first for SEO/LCP.

### Architecture diagram

wide760PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
│
├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
│ SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
│ post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
│
├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
│ Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
│ never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
│ an MRT preview endpoint.
│
├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
│ srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
│
└──◄ Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
HMAC-verified with a shared secret.

### **API surface & token boundary**

| Surface | Origin / Boundary | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | SSR-first; browser hydrates from SSR payload. Safe to embed in bundle. |
| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Editor preview via iframe `postMessage`. Never reaches browser. |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI host only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT/bundle — build-time only. Never embedded, never in PR diffs. |
| Publish webhook | Contentful → MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish. TTL fallback 60s SWR. Rejected and logged if HMAC fails. |

**Key behaviours confirmed in** `02-contentful.md`**:**

* **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
* **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries, the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
* **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
* **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint. `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head.
* **SSR cache TTL.** 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache — the TTL is the fallback if a webhook drops.
* **CDN rate limit.** 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic — risk only during burst republish events.
* **Bundle weight.** Rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
* **No PII** flows through Contentful.

### Content Ownership (from 02-contentful.md)

SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001).

| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
| Size guides | — | Fallback content only. Primary size guide is Measmerize overlay (PRD-053). Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists. | Confirmed |

SFCC Product & Category ID Reference Pattern in Contentful
----------------------------------------------------------

This section documents the resolved design for how SFCC product and category IDs are embedded in Contentful content models, how MRT resolves them at render time, and how conditional component rendering is implemented based on those IDs. This is the core design question the spike(SFCC-123) was tasked to answer.

### Content Model: How to Store SFCC IDs

SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain Short Text fields on the Contentful content type. They are not localized — they are structural fields that identify what SFCC data the editorial entry is associated with, and the value does not change per locale.

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Field Name** | **Field Type** | **Localized** | **Applies To** | **Description** |
| sfccCategoryId | Short Text | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | The SFCC category ID (e.g. womens-dresses) this entry is scoped to. If null, the entry is shown on all categories of that type. |
| sfccProductId | Short Text | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | The SFCC product ID (master product ID) this entry is scoped to. If null, shown on all PDPs. |
| sfccProductIds | Short Text (list) | No | Campaign editorial, Homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. |
| sfccCategoryIds | Short Text (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. |

*Authoring rule: content authors set sfccCategoryId / sfccProductId in Contentful. They do not need to know anything about how MRT resolves it — that logic lives entirely in the SSR layer.*

### Schema-as-Code Definition

Each content type that supports ID-based targeting must include the relevant field in its scripts/contentful/content-types/\*.js definition. Example for PLP Inline Grid Insert:

wide760true{
id: 'sfccCategoryId',
name: 'SFCC Category ID',
type: 'Symbol',          // Short Text in Contentful UI
localized: false,
required: false,
validations: []
}

### Render-Time Resolution in MRT (SSR)

At SSR time, MRT fetches all published entries of a given content type for the current locale via CDA. Before passing entries to React components, the SSR layer filters them by matching the SFCC ID field against the current page context. The component never sees unmatched entries — it receives only the entries that should render.

**Resolution logic by page context:**

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Page Context** | **ID Source** | **Match Logic** |
| PLP (category page) | Route param / SFCC category API response | Filter CDA entries where sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId OR sfccCategoryId is null (show-on-all). |
| PDP (product page) | Route param productId (master product ID) | Filter CDA entries where sfccProductId === currentProductId OR sfccProductId is null. |
| Homepage | No SFCC ID context | No ID filtering — all entries for the slot are rendered in authored order. |
| Campaign landing | Slug / experience ID | Filtered by Contentful Studio Experience — no SFCC ID filtering needed. |

**Pseudocode — MRT SSR filter (PLP example):**

const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({   content\_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',   locale: currentLocale, });  const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter(entry => {   const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;   // null = show on all categories; specific ID = scoped render   return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId; });  // Only matched entries are passed to the component return <PlpInlineGridInsert entries={matchedInserts} />;

### Cache Key Requirements

This is a critical implication of the ID-based filtering pattern. If SSR cache keys do not include the SFCC category or product ID, the cached response for one category will be incorrectly served to a different category.

*Cache key rule: any page whose SSR output depends on sfccCategoryId filtering MUST include the category ID in its MRT cache key. Same rule applies to sfccProductId on PDPs. Failure to do this will cause editorial components to appear on the wrong category/product pages.*

**Cache key construction:**

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Page** | **Cache Key Must Include** |
| PLP | locale + categoryId + (page number if paginated) |
| PDP | locale + productId |
| Homepage | locale only (no SFCC ID context) |

### Component Contract

React components that render SFCC-ID-targeted content must be written to the following contract:

* The component does NOT receive raw Contentful entries — it receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer.
* The component does NOT contain any SFCC ID comparison logic.
* The component renders all entries it receives, in the order it receives them.
* If the entries array is empty (no match), the component renders nothing — null return, no DOM output.

This keeps the component reusable across different SFCC ID scopes without modification.

### Null / Unscoped Behaviour

A Contentful entry with sfccCategoryId = null (field left empty by the author) is treated as "show on all categories" for that content type. This is the default authoring state. Authors only populate the ID field when they want to restrict the component to a specific category or product.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **sfccCategoryId value** | **Render behaviour** |
| null (empty) | Show on all PLPs of this content type |
| "womens-dresses" | Show only on the womens-dresses PLP |
| "mens-shirts" | Show only on the mens-shirts PLP |

## Bottom line up front

Your literal SFCC-238 question — *"what hook do we call, how do we find the hooks, how do we pass the keys"* — **already has a working answer in the codebase for the single-product case**: it's `useProduct` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`, called inside the Contentful leaf component, keyed on a plain Contentful `productId` string. So the spike is **not** greenfield discovery. It's needed to *formalise that pattern into a design decision and close four real gaps around it* — category references, multi-product references, the new SFCC connector app's field shape, and a direct conflict with the repo's own architecture rules. That's exactly the kind of "one problem" a TSD exists to pin down.

---

## 1. Jira state

- **[SFCC-238](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-238)** "Contentful-to-PWA Kit Product/Category ID Rendering (Hook Integration)" — Spike, **To Do**, assigned to you, **created today (2026-07-24)**, parent epic SFCC-1. - **[SFCC-123](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-123)** "Contentful Integration Technical Design & Content Model" — Spike, **Code Review** (Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz). This is the broad parent spike. - Sibling spikes: [SFCC-237](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-237) (MRT app architecture) and [SFCC-122](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-122) (MRT API capabilities), also yours, also in progress.

## 2. Confluence state

- **The SFCC-123 TSD page (346783750) is written and in review** — and it already has a section literally titled *"SFCC Product & Category ID Reference Pattern in Contentful."* **But read closely, that section only covers page-scoping filtering** — "show this editorial banner only on the `womens-dresses` PLP" via an SSR filter (`sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId`). It explicitly makes the React component *dumb* (receives pre-filtered entries, contains no ID logic).
- What it does **not** answer is SFCC-238's actual question: how a product/category ID *embedded in an entry* gets turned into **rendered commerce data** (name, price, image, add-to-bag). It waves at it once — *"Product and category references… are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001)"* — but names no hook, no fetch location, no key-passing mechanic.
- **The rendering/caching strategy is actively contested.** Tim's review comment on the page: *"we need to re-think this approach given we are rendering a lot of required content from Contentful… Let's take a look at the Cache and how often we invalidate."* Another comment confirms Sprint-2 content types are *assumed, not confirmed*.

The integration is **real and substantial**, not a stub — and a product-ID→hook bridge **already works today**:

| Bridge | File | Mechanic |
|---|---|---|
| **ProductHero** (single featured product) | [productHero.tsx:16](overrides/app/components/contentful/productHero.tsx) | Contentful string field → `useProduct({parameters:{id: productHero, allImages:true}}, {enabled:!!productHero})` |

- The key convention is codified: **`SFCC_PRODUCT_ID_FIELD = 'productId'`** ([contentfulMapping.ts:65](overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts)), `Hotspot.productId` ([types/contentful.ts:59](overrides/app/types/contentful.ts)), documented in [shoppableImage.js](scripts/contentful/content-types/shoppableImage.js) as an SFCC **master** product ID.

- **No category bridge at all.** `useCategory`, `useCategories`, `useShopperProducts`, `useProducts`, and Contentful-driven `useProductSearch` — **zero usages** in `overrides/`. 1. **The existing bridge violates the repo's own architecture rule.** `useProduct` is called *inside leaf components* under `overrides/app/components/contentful/`. But [.claude/rules/components.md](.claude/rules/components.md) (container/presentational) says: *"Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props — it does not call data-fetching hooks itself (SDK hooks like… `useProduct`…)."* The current code contradicts the sanctioned pattern. The TSD has to rule: is this a blessed exception, or does resolution move to an SSR/container layer?

2. **CSR hook vs SSR-first mandate — this is Tim's comment.** `useProduct` is a client-side React Query hook resolving *after* hydration. The SFCC-123 TSD mandates **SSR-first** rendering for SEO/LCP, and AGENTS.md sets a hard **≤2s p75 mobile LCP budget**. A product reference resolved client-side inside editorial content is exactly the caching/rendering tension Tim flagged. The decision (SCAPI fetch in SSR and pass down vs. CSR hook vs. hybrid) is a real architectural fork — the kind an options-driven TSD is built to resolve.

3. **The newly-installed SFCC connector app changes the input shape.** Your prompt opens with *"now that we have the Contentful App installed for SFCC."* The existing bridge was built against a **mock space using plain string / JSON fields**. The connector app emits a **structured reference field**, not a bare string — so the `productId`-string convention has to be reconciled with the connector's actual output. That reconciliation is unwritten.

4. **Unresolved upstream ownership.** HPC-001 leaves *whether product names/prices live in Contentful or SFCC* open. The bridge assumes "IDs in Contentful, everything else from SFCC" — correct, but not formally confirmed. A TSD closes it.

So the deliverable is a focused, 8-section TSD (per the [official template](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/352419841), Section 8 sign-off) answering one problem: **how a Contentful-authored product/category reference resolves to rendered PWA data** — which hook (`useProduct` today; `useCategory`/`useProductSearch` for the category gap), where it's called (leaf vs SSR container), how the connector field maps to the hook key, and how that satisfies the SSR-first/LCP and container/presentational rules. content.text:
**In a nutshell:** A content editor drops a product into a Contentful entry (a homepage spotlight, a Shop-the-Look hotspot). All Contentful actually stores is the SFCC **product ID** — not the name, price, or image. This spike pins down *how the PWA turns that bare ID into a live, rendered product tile*.

The mechanic already works for one case — `useProduct(id)` called inside the Contentful component. So the spike isn't "figure it out from scratch." It's **make it an official, reusable pattern and close the gaps:**

1. **Where does the hook belong?** Today it's called *inside a leaf component*, which breaks our own container/presentational rule (data-fetching lives in pages/containers, not leaves) — and it fetches client-side, which fights our SSR-first / LCP budget. Pick the sanctioned approach and write it down.
2. **Categories** — no equivalent exists yet. A Contentful entry pointing at a *category* has nothing wiring it to `useCategory`/`useProductSearch`. Greenfield.
3. **The new SFCC connector app** hands you a structured reference field, not the plain string the current code assumes. Reconcile the two.
4. **Confirm the boundary** — Contentful = IDs + editorial; SFCC = all commerce data. (Still officially open per HPC-001.)

**Output:** one signed-off TSD that every future "editor embedded a product/category" feature (product spotlights, Shop-the-Look, PLP inserts, mega-menu tiles) can just follow — so nobody re-litigates the hook wiring each time.
